newsitem.title: INDIA: India industrial growth to be above 10 pct - ministry.
newsitem.headline: India industrial growth to be above 10 pct - ministry.

text.p: Fears of a slowdown in India's industrial growth rate are overdone, and manfacturing growth remains a driving force in the economy, Industry Secretary N. Mohanty said on Thursday.
Interviewed on Doordashan, India's state-run television channel, Mohanty said industrial growth would end this financial year 1996/97 (April/March) above ten percent.
"My assessment is that it (industrial growth) will remain double-digit by the end of this year, 1996/97," the industry secretary said.
He said the government was still hoped for an outturn close to its 12 percent target, just below the 12.1 percent notched in 1995/96.
"One cannot be so sure at this stage. We are still targetting at 12 percent...it will be around that, definitely a double digit figure," Mohanty said.
Business leaders told Reuters earlier this week that the government was being too optimistic and said they expected industrial output around eight percent this financial year.
Talk of a slowdown in growth had aroused some worries, Mohanty said, but he was optimistic that the economy would regather momentum.
"Well, we are concerned, I mean there is some kind, somewhat of a slowdown.

"But you must remember that between April to September the manufacturing growth has been more than 10 percent. Now it is true that industrial growth which was around 12 percent last year during this period has been around eight percent."
He said industrial growth comprises manufacturing, mining and electricy generation and it was in the latter two areas that the slowdown occurred.
"In manufacturing growth remained more than 10 percent," he said.
And he said softening interest rates, good agricultural sector growth and easing infrastructure problems will help industrial growth stay above 10 percent.
The government has already taken steps to address the main factors hindering growth.
"The government has taken steps to soften interest rates."
"(Bank's) reserve ratio has been brought down and government borrowing has come down with the result that the interest rates have started coming down."
The Reserve Bank of India is expected to make two half-percentage point cuts this month to bring banks Cash Reserve Requirement (CRR) down to 10 percent and pave the way for lower interest rates.
Prime lending rates range between 14.5 and 15 percent, although the average inflation rate over the past six months is around six percent.

He said the high growth rates of the past three to four years had put a strain on India's infrastructure, but the ministries responsible for power, roads and ports were trying to improve the situation.
And he said his own ministry was active trying to ease the path for foreign direct investment.
